context.locality: Toyota City (formerly Fujioka Town), Aichi Prefecture, Japan

evidence.atlas_notes: About 20 larvae from a persimmon orchard, January 2002, reared at 25 C, 15L:9D; nine females emerged and all were extracted, 1-2 days old, calling 12-15 h after lights on. Titre 'about 2 ng/female' from five 1-female-equivalent GC-MS runs (N = 5). Geometry from retention on DB-23 (KI 2639) against all four 3,13 isomers; the authors note the EI spectra of the isomers are quite similar, and the diagnostic ions suggested the 3,13 positions. Negatives: no peaks at the retention times of the other three 3,13 acetates, E2,Z13-18:OAc, E3,Z13- and Z3,Z13-18:OH, or E2,Z13-18:Al (Fig. 2). Z2,Z13- and E2,E13-18:OAc are not recorded as negatives: their standards elute at or beside the Z3,Z13-18:OAc peak in Fig. 2a, so retention alone cannot exclude them (Atlas reading). Atlas note: Korean S. tenuis glands showed the reverse, Z3,Z13-18:OH present and Z3,Z13-18:OAc absent below about 100 pg (spa.obs.synanthedon_tenuis.yang_2012.gland).
evidence.author_statement: The extract included only Z3,Z13-18:OAc, but no alcohols or aldehydes were detected.

evidence.atlas_notes: Larvae collected from persimmon at Gimhae, summers 2010-2011, reared; 1-2-day-old females extracted during peak calling (7th-9th hour of photophase). Fig. 1 marks where synthetic Z3,Z13-18:OAc elutes on both columns: no peak. A tested negative with a stated detection limit.
evidence.author_statement: No additional compounds having pheromone-type structures were detected in the gland extracts (ca. 100 pg of detection limit)

evidence.atlas_notes: Test IV, Motosu, 27 May - 28 September 2004, N = 8, t test P < 0.001. Mean +- SE per trap: 4.6 +- 0.8 vs 17.0 +- 3.8. Atlas note: in Korea the alcohol is the pheromone and the acetate inhibits (spa.obs.synanthedon_tenuis.yang_2012.*). Traps 1.5 m up, rotated after each count, checked about weekly; log(x + 0.5) transformed, one-way ANOVA with Tukey-Kramer HSD or t test; control treatments that caught nothing were left out of the analyses. Shin-Etsu acetates and the authors' synthetic isomers stated above 98 percent pure; alcohols made by saponifying the acetates, purity not stated.
evidence.author_statement: Addition of 10 % Z3,Z13-18:OH to Z3,Z13-18:OAc significantly decreased male captures (Table 4).
